claims.claim: The fixed-k problems are monotone under padding: k-Induced Disjoint Paths reduces to ℓ-Induced Disjoint Paths for every fixed ℓ≥k while preserving H3-freeness. Moreover, k=1 is linear-time solvable and every fixed-k problem is in NP.
claims.evidence: For ℓ−k new pairs, add disjoint isolated K2 components and use their endpoints as terminals. Every added pair must use its isolated edge, so restriction and extension are inverse solution maps. Since H3 is connected and has eight vertices, adding K2 components preserves H3-subgraph-freeness. For k=1, an instance is positive exactly when its terminals are connected; BFS or DFS decides this in O(n+m), and a shortest connecting path is induced. For fixed k, k simple paths have polynomial total description length, and their endpoints, edges, vertex-disjointness, chords, and inter-path adjacencies are polynomially verifiable.
claims.witness: The explicit padding witness consists of ℓ−k isolated terminal edges, one for every new pair.
claims.search_method: Direct proof from the source definitions, including both directions of the padding equivalence and certificate-size verification.

claims.claim: Every H3-free graph is 6-degenerate, with the constant sharp; additionally, two vertices of degree at least three can never be at distance exactly three. Thus an n-vertex H3-free graph has at most 6n−21 edges for n≥7, and every connected H3-free graph of minimum degree at least three has diameter at most two.
claims.evidence: If degree-at-least-three vertices u and v have distance three, take a geodesic u-x-y-v and two additional neighbors of each endpoint. Shortestness excludes all connector-vertex coincidences and any common additional neighbor would give distance at most two. These eight distinct vertices and seven selected edges form H3 as a subgraph. For degeneracy, any subgraph of minimum degree at least seven contains every eight-vertex tree: embed a rooted tree parent-first; when its jth vertex is embedded, its parent has at most j−2≤6 already occupied neighbors and hence an unused neighbor. Thus such a subgraph contains H3, proving 6-degeneracy. K7 is H3-free and 6-degenerate, proving sharpness. A 6-degeneracy ordering contributes at most six forward edges from its first n−7 vertices and at most 21 among its last seven, yielding 6n−21. Finally, a geodesic of length at least three has first and fourth vertices at distance exactly three, contradicting the distance lemma when minimum degree is at least three.
claims.witness: K7 has seven vertices, degeneracy six, and 21=6·7−21 edges, while H3 requires eight distinct vertices.
claims.search_method: Direct extremal and metric proofs, supplemented by an exact checker for the H3 and K7 finite witnesses.

claims.claim: H3-free graphs admit an arbitrary-routing-plus-matching normal form. Let R be any graph and M a matching on V(R), disjoint from E(R). Replace every edge of R by a four-edge path and retain every edge of M unsubdivided, obtaining G(R,M). Then G(R,M) is H3-free. With all terminals in V(R), induced linkages in G(R,M) correspond exactly to vertex-disjoint paths in R∪M such that every M-edge whose two endpoints are selected is itself used between consecutive vertices of one path. In particular, the H3-free class has unbounded treewidth.
claims.evidence: Every subdivision vertex has degree two, so an H3 center would have to be original. A simple three-edge path starting at an original vertex either starts down an R-corridor and ends at its third subdivision vertex, or first uses its unique possible M-edge and then, because M is a matching and the path is simple, takes two corridor edges and again ends at a subdivision vertex. Hence no three-edge path joins two possible centers and H3 cannot occur. A path with original endpoints that enters a corridor must traverse it completely because its three internal vertices have degree two. Contracting traversed corridors therefore produces a simple path in R∪M, and lifting base paths reverses the contraction while preserving vertex-disjointness. Corridor interiors have no outside neighbors and unused R-edges are not host adjacencies between their original endpoints. Consequently the only possible extra edge among selected vertices is an unsubdivided M-edge, which is harmless exactly when it is a consecutive used edge of one path. This proves the stated exact correspondence. With M empty and R=K_m, contracting every corridor gives a K_m minor, so treewidth is at least m−1 and is unbounded.
claims.witness: The family G(K_m,∅) is H3-free and contains K_m as a minor for every m.
claims.search_method: Direct degree and path-contraction proof; additionally exhausted 328 pairs (R,M) with |V(R)|≤4 and 4145 lifted one- and two-path families.

claims.claim: For arbitrary graphs, hence also for H3-free graphs, k-Induced Disjoint Paths is fixed-parameter tractable in k+b, where b is the number of vertices of degree at least three. There is an exact equivalent compression with at most b+binom(b,2)+6k vertices.
claims.evidence: Let B contain the b vertices of degree at least three. Each component of G−B is a path, isolated vertex, or unattached cycle; a path component has at most two attachment edges because only its endpoints can have outside neighbors. A terminal-free component used by a terminal path must be entered and exited through two distinct B vertices. Components with fewer attachments or two attachments to the same B vertex cannot be used by a simple terminal path, and all terminal-free corridors with the same distinct endpoints are interchangeable; one length-two representative per unordered B-pair suffices, using at most binom(b,2) vertices. In a terminal-bearing path component, mark its terminals and its zero, one, or two B attachment occurrences. In a cycle, mark its terminals; a detached cycle with exactly one terminal makes the instance immediately negative. Between consecutive marks, every internal vertex has degree two, is nonterminal, and has no external neighbor, so a solution either traverses the whole gap or uses none of its interior. A one-edge gap must remain an edge because its boundary marks are adjacent; every gap of length at least two can be replaced by a two-edge path because its boundary marks are nonadjacent. Contraction and expansion therefore preserve exactly all linkage constraints. A path component with t≥1 terminals has at most t+1≤2t gaps and a cycle has t gaps. Across at most 2k terminal occurrences this requires at most 4k internal gap representatives, while B and the terminals require at most b+2k vertices. The total is at most b+binom(b,2)+6k. The compression is polynomial-time constructible, and exhaustive enumeration on its parameter-bounded vertex set gives f(k+b)·n^O(1) time.
claims.witness: The proof supplies mutually inverse contraction and expansion maps for every retained corridor and marked gap; the implementation independently preserved the answer and size bound on every tested instance.
claims.search_method: Constructive compression proof plus exhaustive exact comparison on 100490 labelled instances: k=1 through six vertices, k=2 on four through six vertices, and k=3 on six vertices.

claims.claim: A globally shortest path for one terminal pair cannot be fixed greedily, even on a seven-vertex H3-free graph.
claims.evidence: On vertices s1,t1,x,s2,t2,y,z with edges s1x,xt1,xs2,s2t2,s1y,yz,zt1, the graph is H3-free because H3 has eight vertices. Exact path enumeration shows that s1-x-t1 is the unique globally shortest s1-t1 path. Every s2-t2 path contains s2, and the edge xs2 consequently prevents any induced linkage containing that shortest path. Nevertheless, s1-y-z-t1 together with s2-t2 is a valid induced linkage: the paths are vertex-disjoint, individually induced, and have no edge between them.
claims.witness: Vertices {s1,t1,x,s2,t2,y,z}; edges {s1x,xt1,xs2,s2t2,s1y,yz,zt1}; valid paths s1-y-z-t1 and s2-t2.
claims.search_method: Complete exact enumeration of the relevant simple induced paths and all selected-vertex adjacencies in the seven-vertex graph.

target_evidence: The exact target requests a complexity classification for every fixed k on H3-subgraph-free graphs. The draft proves a linear-time classification only for k=1 and explicitly leaves every fixed k≥2 unclassified; neither the k+b algorithm nor the routing normal form supplies a fixed-k polynomial-time algorithm or hardness result when b is unbounded. Thus the draft makes correct, material progress but does not resolve the full requested classification. Its claimed_resolution is PARTIAL and its final writeup repeatedly states this limitation, so that claimed resolution is accurate rather than overstated or understated.
